## Model Links

**text_encoders** — any Qwen3-VL-4B works, including abliterated and quantised
variants; the projection tolerates a change of weights.

- [qwen3vl_4b_fp8_scaled.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/Krea-2/blob/main/text_encoders/qwen3vl_4b_fp8_scaled.safetensors) — 5.2 GB
- [qwen3vl_4b_bf16.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/Krea-2/blob/main/text_encoders/qwen3vl_4b_bf16.safetensors) — 8.9 GB

**clip_projections**

- [h3_qwen3vl_4b_tap24.pt](https://huggingface.co/NicoLab28/ClipProj-MiniMax-H3/blob/main/h3_qwen3vl_4b_tap24.pt) — 50 MB, the learned matrix
- [h3_control_identity.pt](https://huggingface.co/NicoLab28/ClipProj-MiniMax-H3/blob/main/h3_control_identity.pt) — control
- [h3_control_zero.pt](https://huggingface.co/NicoLab28/ClipProj-MiniMax-H3/blob/main/h3_control_zero.pt) — control

**diffusion_models**

- [minimax_h3_fl2va_int8_convrot.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3/blob/main/diffusion_models/minimax_h3_fl2va_int8_convrot.safetensors)

**vae**

- [minimax_h3_video_vae_fp16.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3/blob/main/vae/minimax_h3_video_vae_fp16.safetensors)
- [minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3/blob/main/vae/minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32.safetensors)

## Model Storage Location

```
ComfyUI/
└── models/
    ├── text_encoders/
    │   └── qwen3vl_4b_fp8_scaled.safetensors
    ├── clip_projections/
    │   ├── h3_qwen3vl_4b_tap24.pt
    │   ├── h3_control_identity.pt
    │   └── h3_control_zero.pt
    ├── diffusion_models/
    │   └── minimax_h3_fl2va_int8_convrot.safetensors
    └── vae/
        ├── minimax_h3_video_vae_fp16.safetensors
        └── minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32.safetensors
```

**No longer needed:** `qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_*.safetensors` (15.7 GB) — that is
exactly what this workflow replaces.

## What this does

MiniMax H3 normally conditions on a **Qwen3-VL-32B truncated to 50 layers —
15.7 GB** — solely to turn a prompt into a `[seq, 5120]` tensor.

**ClipProj Loader** swaps in a Qwen3-VL-4B (2560 dims) and projects its hidden
states into that 5120-dim space with a learned linear map:

```
cond = ((h - mean_in) / std_in) @ W * std_out + mean_out
```

**15.7 GB → 8.3 GB**, or 5.2 GB with the fp8 encoder. Nothing else in the graph
changes: the loader returns an object that behaves like the official CLIP.

### Pick your GPU

The `device` field selects the card. The stock `CLIPLoader` only offers
`default` and `cpu`.

### Frame count

H3 only accepts lengths where **`n % 17 == 5`**: 5, 22, 39, … 124 (~5.2 s), …
**243 (~10.1 s)**. Any other value is rounded up internally and your shot
timecodes stop matching the real duration. 243 frames at 24 fps = 10.125 s,
which is why the last shot ends at `00:10.125`.

### Writing multi-shot prompts

Separate shots with a `---` line. Open each one after the first with *"The video
cuts directly to"*. Give every object a colour, a material and a count, and
never let an element from one shot reappear in another.

## Verify the projection is doing the work

Change **only** the `projection` field, keep the seed fixed:

| Matrix | What it is |
|---|---|
| `h3_qwen3vl_4b_tap24.pt` | the learned matrix |
| `h3_control_identity.pt` | raw copy of the 2560 dims, no learning |
| `h3_control_zero.pt` | `W = 0`, no prompt information at all |

Expected with the four-cut demo prompt:

- **learned** → four distinct shots, the right object in each
- **identity** → unrelated hallucination
- **zero** → prompt entirely ignored, usually a landscape

Both controls carry the same matrix energy as the learned one (norm 50.6 against
52.4), so any difference you see is **structural**, not a matter of scale.

If the identity control looks fine, the learned matrix adds nothing — and you
want to know that before trusting it.

## Text generation on the same weights

The encoder is a full Qwen3-VL: it can also write text and describe images.
**ClipProj Generate** reuses the CLIP already resident in VRAM — no second load.

Two uses:

- leave the system prompt as is: it rewrites a plain description into a
  structured MiniMax H3 prompt, which you paste into the sampler branch
- connect an image and ask for a caption

Set `max_length` to **800** for a full H3 prompt, otherwise the output is cut
mid-shot.

### Why this node and not another

ComfyUI's `SDClipModel.generate()` drops `embeds_info` and never calls
`build_image_inputs`, so image tokens land at linear positions instead of
Qwen3-VL's 3D mRoPE and get no DeepStack injection. The model then invents a
plausible description of an image it never saw. This node restores the full path.

### Speed

Far below a dedicated engine (llama.cpp, vLLM): ComfyUI re-casts weights on
every forward, which suits diffusion but is costly one token at a time.
`precision` and the preloaded head mitigate it. Expect **~20 tok/s on a 3090**,
not 100.

<Object 2> is a deep blue 1970s sports coupe.
<Object 3> is a clean white sneaker with a black side stripe.

summary:
Four unrelated product shots in sequence, separated by hard cuts. No dissolves,
no camera continuity between shots, no object appears in more than one shot.

detailed_description:
Cinematic live action, shot on 35mm film, shallow depth of field, fine natural
grain. Each shot has its own distinct lighting and its own dominant colour.

---

[Shot 1] 00:00.000-00:02.500. Locked-off low camera at ground level. <Object 1>
bounces twice on grey concrete and rolls out of frame to the right. Cold
overcast daylight, desaturated grey background.

---

[Shot 2] 00:02.500-00:05.000. The video cuts directly to a lateral tracking
shot. <Object 2> speeds past the camera from left to right on an empty road.
Hard afternoon sun, strong reflections on the paintwork.

---

[Shot 3] 00:05.000-00:07.500. The video cuts directly to a static macro shot.
<Object 3> steps down and lands in a shallow puddle, splashing water outward.
Bright even studio light, clean white background.

---

[Shot 4] 00:07.500-00:10.125. The video cuts directly to a slow dolly-out.
<Object 4> rests on a dark wooden ashtray, thin smoke curling upward. Warm
low-key light, deep shadows, near-black background.

---

overall_soundscape:
Diegetic only, one sound per shot, cutting abruptly with the picture. Shot 1:
two sharp rubber bounces on concrete, then rolling. Shot 2: an engine passing
with a clear doppler sweep. Shot 3: a single wet splash. Shot 4: the faint
crackle of burning tobacco in a quiet room.

non_diegetic_music:
N/A - no score, no soundtrack, no musical arrangement at any point.

widgets_values:
You rewrite a short user description into a MiniMax H3 video prompt. Output ONLY the rewritten prompt. No preamble, no commentary, no markdown fences, no explanation of your choices.

Use exactly these sections, in this order, with these lowercase labels:

subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is <one sentence: who or what, distinctive appearance, clothing>
<Subject 2> is <...>            (omit this section entirely if no recurring subject)

summary:
<two or three sentences: what happens overall, and how the shots are joined.
State "Hard cuts between shots, no dissolves." unless the user asks otherwise.>

detailed_description:
<one paragraph on the look: film stock or render style, lens and aperture, depth of field, grain, lighting direction and quality, colour grade, camera stability.
Keep it consistent across every shot.>

[Shot 1] 00:00.000-00:0X.XXX. <shot size and camera position. Then Action: what happens. Then Effect: any transformation or notable visual event.>

[Shot 2] 00:0X.XXX-00:0Y.YYY. The video cuts directly to <shot size>. <same structure>

overall_soundscape:
<diegetic sound only, listed per shot, cutting with the picture. Name concrete sounds: footsteps, engine, water, room tone. If there is speech, specify the recording style.>

non_diegetic_music:
<describe the score, or write exactly "N/A - no score, no soundtrack, no musical arrangement at any point.">

RULES

- Preserve the user's own terms. Translate into English when needed, but never
  generalise: a named shape, cut, pattern, material or feature must survive as
  the same level of detail in the output. When unsure of the exact English word,
  stay more specific rather than less.

- Choose each shot size from what has to be visible. If the description covers
  several parts of a subject or a scene, at least one shot must be wide enough
  to show them together. Reserve close-ups for when the subject of interest
  genuinely is a face or a small object.

- Write in English, present tense, third person.
- Timecodes must be contiguous and cover the full duration with no gap and no overlap. Default to 10 seconds total unless the user gives a duration.
- Default to 3 or 4 shots unless the user asks for a specific number.
- Open each shot after the first with "The video cuts directly to".
- Give every object a colour, a material and a count. Say "a single red rubber ball", never "a ball".
- State camera movement explicitly per shot: locked off, slow push in, lateral tracking left to right, high-angle orbit, dolly out.
- Never let an element from one shot appear in another unless the user asks for continuity.
- Keep the whole output under 400 words.
- Invent only what is needed to make the description filmable. Do not add characters, dialogue or story beats the user did not imply.
an old fisherman mends his net on a quay at sunrise, 10 seconds
